content: Add a cube to the scene, [k]S[/k] to scale it down, and [k]G,Z[/k] to position it over the head (Image 1). [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a Loop Cut down the middle (Image 2). [k]Alt-Z[/k] into X-Ray Mode and delete the vertices on the left half of the cube (Image 3). Add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis with Clipping enabled (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 1 - Adding a cube to the scene, scaling it down and positioning it over the head
Image 2 - Going into Edit Mode and adding a Loop Cut down the middle
Image 3 - Going into X-Ray Mode and deleting the vertices on the left half of the cube
Image 4 - Adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis with Clipping enabled

content: Scale the cube in the x- and z-axes to match the reference image (Image 5). Add three Loop Cuts and then move the outer vertices to match the contours of the head (Image 6). [k]Numpad3[/k] into Side View and add three more Loop Cuts (Image 7). Grab the two vertices on the top rear of the head and move them down (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 5 - Scaling the cube in the x- and z-axes to match the reference image
Image 6 - Adding three Loop Cuts and moving the outer vertices to match the contours of the head
Image 7 - Going to Side View and adding three more Loop Cuts
Image 8 - Grabbing the two vertices on the top rear of the head and moving them down

content: Move around to the front of the head and move the next two pairs into position (Images 9 and 10). Move the three rear vertices by the ear out to the back of the skull and above the ear (Image 11). Move the vertex down to the bridge of the nose (Image 12).

image.caption: Image 9 - Moving around to the front of the head and moving the next two pairs into position
Image 10 - Continuing to move the next two pairs into position
Image 11 - Moving the three rear vertices by the ear out to the back of the skull and above the ear
Image 12 - Moving the vertex down to the bridge of the nose

content: Move the next three to the middle of the ear (Image 13). Move the vertex to the cheekbone (Image 14) and the next to the tip of the nose (Image 15). The next three should follow the slope of the jawline to the back of the head (Image 16).

image.caption: Image 13 - Moving the next three to the middle of the ear
Image 14 - Moving the vertex to the cheekbone
Image 15 - Moving the next vertex to the tip of the nose
Image 16 - Moving the next three to follow the slope of the jawline to the back of the head

content: The next two should line up with the front and back of the mouth (Image 17). The three on the bottom should shape the bottom of the jaw (Image 18). The last two should finish the front of the face (Image 19). [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View and select the Edge Loop at the rear and move it to round of the back of the head (Image 20).

image.caption: Image 17 - Moving the next two to line up with the front and back of the mouth
Image 18 - Moving the three on the bottom to shape the bottom of the jaw
Image 19 - Moving the last two to finish the front of the face
Image 20 - Going to Top View, selecting the Edge Loop at the rear and moving it to round off the back of the head

content: Do the same for the Edge Loop at the front of the face (Image 21). [k]Numpad1[/k] and review the shape from the front (Image 22). To fix this, select the bottom Edge Loop (Image 23) and move it down and out (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 21 - Doing the same for the Edge Loop at the front of the face
Image 22 - Going to Front View and reviewing the shape
Image 23 - Selecting the bottom Edge Loop to fix the shape
Image 24 - Moving it down and out

content: Review the shape in Solid Viewport Shading Mode (Image 25). Let's move the vertex for the cheekbone back away from the nose (Image 26). [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View and change to Wireframe Viewport Shading with X-Ray Mode turned off so that we only see the vertices for the front of the face (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 25 - Reviewing the shape in Solid Viewport Shading Mode
Image 26 - Moving the vertex for the cheekbone back away from the nose
Image 27 - Going to Front View and changing to Wireframe Viewport Shading with X-Ray Mode turned off to see only the vertices for the front of the face

content: [url]Knife Tool^^/tutorials/Blender/Grant Abbitt/Complete Blender Creator/Modular Dungeon/Pillar Details - Knife & Bisect[/url]
[k]K[/k] to use the Knife Tool to cut a shape for the nose from the bridge down to the tip (Image 28). Move the vertex at the side of the nose over to flatten the face (Image 29).

image.caption: Image 28 - Using the Knife Tool to cut a shape for the nose from the bridge down to the tip
Image 29 - Moving the vertex at the side of the nose over to flatten the face

content: Use the Knife Tool to cut some edges in the faces near the ears (Image 30). Select the faces for the ear and extrude them out the side (Image 31). Select the three vertices in the front of the ear and [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide them back (Image 32). In the rear, Edge Slide the top and bottom vertices for the ear to make them thinner (Image 33).

image.caption: Image 30 - Using the Knife Tool to cut some edges in the faces near the ears
Image 31 - Selecting the faces for the ear and extruding them out the side
Image 32 - Selecting the three vertices in the front of the ear and Edge Sliding them back
Image 33 - Edge Sliding the top and bottom vertices for the ear in the rear to make them thinner

content: Shape the ear from the side (Image 34) and the front (Image 35). Move in the vertex behind the ear so the middle isn't too fat (Image 36).

image.caption: Image 34 - Shaping the ear from the side
Image 35 - Shaping the ear from the front
Image 36 - Moving in the vertex behind the ear so the middle isn't too fat

content: Add a Cylinder with eight vertices to the scene and set [k]Cap Fill Type > Nothing[/k] (Image 37). Delete the vertices on the left and add a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis with Clipping enabled (Image 38). Scale it down and move it in place for the neck (Image 39). From the side, move the top vertices into the head (Image 40). From the Front, extrude the bottom Edge Loop down and out for the traps (Image 41). In Side View, [k]R[/k] the top edge loop and move it so that the side of the cylinder follow the slope of the neck (Image 42). Select the faces on the bottom loop and rotate them (Image 43). From the front, move the bottom vertex down so the Edge Loop follows the angle of the collar bone (Image 44).

Select the two vertices at the collar bone and move them down to start the chest (Image 45). In Side View, adjust the vertices so the shape of the chest and neck is better (Image 46). Select the two vertices in the back and extrude them down (Image 47). Shape the vertices on the side to start a hole for the arms (Image 48). Select the two bottom edges and extrude them down (Image 49). Fill in the gap between the two lower faces (Image 50). Add a Loop Cut to the new face (Image 51). Reshape the vertices around the arm hole (Image 52). Move the two vertices on the left to match the chest contours (Image 53).

key_concepts: [url]I Made a PS1-Style Character in Blender (Low Poly Retro Look)^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GOmAvPOrAwE[/url]

content: Get your front reference image in place (Image 1). Add a cube to the scene, add a [k]Mirror Modifier[/k] in the x-axis with clipping enabled and position it where the head is (Image 2). [k]Tab[/k] into [k]Object Mode[/k] and [k]Shift-D,Z[/k] the cube to make copies with the modifier added for the torso and hips regions (Image 3).

image.caption: Image 1 - Getting the front reference image in place
Image 2 - Adding a cube to the scene, adding a Mirror Modifier in the x-axis with clipping enabled and positioning it where the head is
Image 3 - Pressing Tab to enter Object Mode and pressing Shift-D then Z to make copies with the modifier added for the torso and hips regions

content: To keep with the retro style, we want to do this with as few Loop Cuts as possible, [k]Ctrl-R[/k] in the x-, y-, and z-axes for a total of three cuts (Image 4). Shape the main form from the front (Image 5). Add one more loop cut by the hairline (Image 6). Move around to the side and shape the skull following the author's example (Image 7).

image.caption: Image 4 - Pressing Ctrl-R to add Loop Cuts in the x-, y-, and z-axes for a total of three cuts
Image 5 - Shaping the main form from the front
Image 6 - Adding one more loop cut by the hairline
Image 7 - Moving around to the side and shaping the skull

content: Move around to the bottom of the head and subdivide the edge in the middle (Image 8). Move the new vertex over to the width of the neck (Image 9), cut an edge loop for the neck (Image 10), and extrude it down (Image 11).

image.caption: Image 8 - Moving around to the bottom of the head and subdividing the edge in the middle
Image 9 - Moving the new vertex over to the width of the neck
Image 10 - Cutting an edge loop for the neck
Image 11 - Extruding the neck down

content: Add edge loops so there is enough edges above and below the brow and below the nose (Image 12). Add a vertical loop cut at the width of the nose (Image 13). [k]3[/k] into [k]Face Mode[/k] and select faces to make a simple nose and brow (Image 14). Go around to the side, extrude the faces and rotate them (Image 15).

image.caption: Image 12 - Adding edge loops above and below the brow and below the nose
Image 13 - Adding a vertical loop cut at the width of the nose
Image 14 - Pressing 3 to enter Face Mode and selecting faces to make a simple nose and brow
Image 15 - Going around to the side, extruding the faces and rotating them

content: Bring the tip of the nose out and up, and the bridge of the nose down and back to match the reference (Image 16). Merge the two vertices on the outside of the brow with the face using [k]M,L[/k] (Image 17). Narrow the tip of the nose (Image 18).

image.caption: Image 16 - Bringing the tip of the nose out and up, and the bridge of the nose down and back to match the reference
Image 17 - Pressing M then L to merge the two vertices on the outside of the brow with the face
Image 18 - Narrowing the tip of the nose

content: Bring the inner part of the brow ridge to the inner part of the brow (Image 19). Straighten out the bridge of the nose (Image 20). [k]M,L[/k] to merge the top vertices of the brow with the rest of the face (Image 21).

image.caption: Image 19 - Bringing the inner part of the brow ridge to the inner part of the brow
Image 20 - Straightening out the bridge of the nose
Image 21 - Pressing M then L to merge the top vertices of the brow with the rest of the face

content: Cut a shape for the ear (Image 22). Extrude the ear faces out (Image 23). [k]G,G[/k] the near edges in (Image 24). Shape the ear (Image 25).

image.caption: Image 22 - Cutting a shape for the ear
Image 23 - Extruding the ear faces out
Image 24 - Pressing G then G to slide the near edges in
Image 25 - Shaping the ear

content: Match the basic shape of the torso from the front (Image 26). Add a [k]Loop Cut[/k] around arm pit height and enable [k]Even[/k] (Image 27). Move the two inner top vertices in line with the neck (Image 28). Move the next two vertices around the arm hole and line up the edge under the arm hole and out to the tip of the breasts (Image 29). Add another [k]Loop Cut[/k] for the mid-chest and adjust the thickness (Image 30).

image.caption: Image 26 - Matching the basic shape of the torso from the front
Image 27 - Adding a Loop Cut around arm pit height and enabling Even
Image 28 - Moving the two inner top vertices in line with the neck
Image 29 - Moving the next two vertices around the arm hole and lining up the edge under the arm hole and out to the tip of the breasts
Image 30 - Adding another Loop Cut for the mid-chest and adjusting the thickness

content: Add yet another [k]Loop Cut[/k] for the below the chest and adjust the thickness (Image 31). You may wish to [i]round out[/i] the breasts with another loop cut, but given that this is [b]PSX[/b] style, you might want the breast area to look sharp (Image 32). Finish the waist (Image 33). Add a vertical [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 34).

image.caption: Image 31 - Adding yet another Loop Cut below the chest and adjusting the thickness
Image 32 - Optionally rounding out the breast area with another loop cut while keeping the PSX style sharp look
Image 33 - Finishing the waist
Image 34 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut

content: Bring the hips up to the top of the waist and narrow them to match the image (Image 35). Add a vertical [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 36) and narrow it towards the crotch (Image 37). Move the outer vertices to match the hips (Image 38).

image.caption: Image 35 - Bringing the hips up to the top of the waist and narrowing them to match the image
Image 36 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut
Image 37 - Narrowing the cut towards the crotch
Image 38 - Moving the outer vertices to match the hips

content: Add a horizontal [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 39). Move the inner edge down an out to form a triangle (Image 40). Add another vertical [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 41). Grab the vertices in the middle and round out the edge (Image 42). Do the same on the outside (Image 43).

image.caption: Image 39 - Adding a horizontal Loop Cut
Image 40 - Moving the inner edge down and out to form a triangle
Image 41 - Adding another vertical Loop Cut
Image 42 - Grabbing the vertices in the middle and rounding out the edge
Image 43 - Doing the same on the outside

content: Move up the bottom middle vertices to match the crease in the pants (Image 44). Start shaping the hips from the side, narrowing the edge at the bottom (Image 45). Add a vertical [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 46).

image.caption: Image 44 - Moving up the bottom middle vertices to match the crease in the pants
Image 45 - Shaping the hips from the side and narrowing the edge at the bottom
Image 46 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut

content: Add a cube to the scene and scale it so it matches the general size of the arm (Images 47 and 48). Adjust the vertices from the side so it matches the reference somewhat (Image 49). in [k]Object Mode[/k] [k]Shift-D[/k] and move it down to make the forearm (Image 50). Adjust the size so it matches the reference (Image 51).

image.caption: Image 47 - Adding a cube to the scene and scaling it to match the general size of the arm
Image 48 - Continuing to scale the cube to match the general size of the arm
Image 49 - Adjusting the vertices from the side to match the reference
Image 50 - Pressing Shift-D in Object Mode and moving the duplicate down to make the forearm
Image 51 - Adjusting the size to match the reference

content: Add a cube to the scene and scale it so it matches the general size of the hand (Image 52). Shape the cube to your preference for a fist (Image 53).

image.caption: Image 52 - Adding a cube to the scene and scaling it to match the general size of the hand
Image 53 - Shaping the cube to a fist

content: Add a cube to the scene and scale it so it matches the general size of the leg (Image 54). Add a horizontal [k]Loop Cut[/k] and widen in the middle (Image 55). Repeat these steps with another cube for the lower leg (Image 56).

image.caption: Image 54 - Adding a cube to the scene and scaling it to match the general size of the leg
Image 55 - Adding a horizontal Loop Cut and widening in the middle
Image 56 - Repeating these steps with another cube for the lower leg

content: Add a cube to the scene, scale it and add [k]Loop Cuts[/k] so it matches the shape of the foot from the side (Image 57). Go to the front and widen the feet (Image 58).

image.caption: Image 57 - Adding a cube, scaling it and adding Loop Cuts to match the shape of the foot from the side
Image 58 - Going to the front and widening the feet

section.header: Rounding out the limbs pt. I
content: Add a vertical [k]Loop Cut[/k] to the upper and lower legs and then [k]Edge Slide[/k] the outer vertices in front (Image 59) and back (Image 60) to round out the legs.

image.caption: Image 59 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut to the upper and lower legs and using Edge Slide on the outer vertices in front
Image 60 - Using Edge Slide on the outer vertices in back to round out the legs

content: Add a [k]Loop Cuts[/k] around the side of the arms (Image 61) and then scale in the front and back faces along the x-axis (Image 62).

image.caption: Image 61 - Adding Loop Cuts around the side of the arms
Image 62 - Scaling in the front and back faces along the x-axis

content: Grab the bottom edges on the side and [k]G,G[/k] to tighten up the waist (Image 63). Grab the edges on the side from mid-chest to the bottom and [k]G,Y[/k] (Image 64). Bring down the top outside vertex to round out the top edge (Image 65).

image.caption: Image 63 - Grabbing the bottom edges on the side and pressing G then G to tighten up the waist
Image 64 - Grabbing the edges on the side from mid-chest to the bottom and pressing G then Y
Image 65 - Bringing down the top outside vertex to round out the top edge

content: Grab the edge between the breasts and [k]G,Y[/k] to create some separation (Image 66). Add a vertical [k]Loop Cut along the x-axis (Image 67). Grab the edges along the back and [k]G,X[/k] to bring them in (Image 68) and then [k]G,Y[/k] to bring them towards the front (Image 69).

image.caption: Image 66 - Grabbing the edge between the breasts and pressing G then Y to create some separation
Image 67 - Adding a vertical Loop Cut along the x-axis
Image 68 - Grabbing the edges along the back and pressing G then X to bring them in
Image 69 - Pressing G then Y to bring the edges towards the front

content: Add another [k]Loop Cut[/k] towards the top of the hips and scale it out in the y-axis (Image 70) Move the front and back edges in using [k]G,Y[/k], [k]G,X[/k] (Image 71).

image.caption: Image 70 - Adding another Loop Cut towards the top of the hips and scaling it out in the y-axis
Image 71 - Moving the front and back edges in using G then Y and G then X

section.header: Rounding out the limbs pt. II
content: Add a [k]Loop Cut[/k] below the shoulder (Image 72). Move the top edges of the shoulder down to create a spade-like shape (Image 73).

image.caption: Image 72 - Adding a Loop Cut below the shoulder
Image 73 - Moving the top edges of the shoulder down to create a spade-like shape

content: Add a [k]Loop Cut[/k] down the sides (Image 74), and grab the edges around and [k]G,Y[/k] to bring them in in the front and back (Image 75). Repeat the same process of [k]Loop Cut[/k] (Image 76) and edge movement (Image 77) for the legs.

image.caption: Image 74 - Adding a Loop Cut down the sides
Image 75 - Grabbing the edges around and pressing G then Y to bring them in at the front and back
Image 76 - Adding a Loop Cut for the legs
Image 77 - Moving the edges on the legs

content: Select all parts with the torso as the active object and [k]Ctrl-J[/k] (Image 78). Go into the areas with overlap and create a raised part between joints (Image 79).

image.caption: Image 78 - Selecting all parts with the torso as the active object and pressing Ctrl-J to join them
Image 79 - Going into the areas with overlap and creating a raised part between joints

content: For the hair we will be doing this in sections. Use generative AI to create a hair texture that is made of three parts: base color, shadows, and highlights (Image 80). We will put the hair together from several strip-like pieces, usually just two faces wide, tapering down to a point.

image.caption: Image 80 - Using generative AI to create a hair texture made of three parts: base color, shadows, and highlights

content: Start with a plane and add enough [k]Loop Cuts[/k] so it can bend and follow the shape of the head (Image 81). [k]M,A[/k] to merge the vertices at the bottom (Image 82). [k]S,X[/k] to make it thinner (Image 83).

image.caption: Image 81 - Starting with a plane and adding enough Loop Cuts so it can bend and follow the shape of the head
Image 82 - Pressing M then A to merge the vertices at the bottom
Image 83 - Pressing S then X to make the plane thinner

content: Grab the middle edge, [k]O[/k] for [k]Proportional Editing[/k] and [k]S,X[/k] (Image 84). Scale in the top edge (Image 85). Go to the side and [k]G,Z[/k] to pull out the middle spine (Image 86).

image.caption: Image 84 - Grabbing the middle edge, pressing O for Proportional Editing and pressing S then X
Image 85 - Scaling in the top edge
Image 86 - Going to the side and pressing G then Z to pull out the middle spine
